steps.name: A Stained Fairy Tale (1)
steps.objective: First talk to [Arche] in 「Pneuma」, then find [Talos] in 「Knossos」.

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: Welcome, %s.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I found the object and returned it to someone in Lumen. I think we can find the next one the same way...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Arche...

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: Yes?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: How did you work that out? How did you know we could find things that way?

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: It's no secret, but I don't really know either. It's hard to explain how...

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: I think I learned it from all the information the spirits have given me during my long time here.

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: If you're that curious, why not stay here for a few centuries?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I am curious, but somehow that doesn't appeal to me.

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: I thought you might say that.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Where should I go this time, Arche?

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: Of the places you've visited recently, which left you with the most questions?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Knossos... It was once part of the beastman empire. A great deal seems to have happened there, but I could learn very little.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Oh, Arche...

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: Yes?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: You visited Freios and Eastland before coming here, didn't you? Have you ever been to Knossos?

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: I don't know. Whether I went and don't remember, or never went at all...

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: I've remembered my time as the Weaver, but not all of it.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Hmm...

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: Still, I'll try to remember as much as I can. Even if not right away... If it helps you, %s...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I'm sorry, Arche. I was only thinking of myself.

lines.speaker: 아르케
lines.text: Not at all. Go and have a look. You may find something out.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I will. Straight to Knossos, then.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Hello, Talos.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: Turning up out of nowhere... You want information from me.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: I said to visit often if you wanted to build trust. Such an obedient little butcher of the goddess.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: (Sigh. Patience. Be patient.)

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I came to ask you something.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: For nothing? Let's help each other. If you want something from me, show your hand.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Here.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: What's this?
(Talos takes the bag from %s with a puzzled look.)

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I picked up litter on the way here from the outpost. Pulled a few weeds too.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: Damn... You've done exactly what I like best...

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: If you've gone that far, I'll at least hear you out.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: (That was surprisingly easy...)

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Then let me ask. Have you lost anything recently?

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: No. Nothing. Satisfied? Off you go.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Wait, wait. Just a moment. Do you know anyone looking for something they've lost?

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: Not something lost recently, but there's something I'd like to find. Though it's hard to call it mine...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: (I think I know what he means... Oh, Narsha!)

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: If there's nothing, then never mind.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: You accepted that rather easily. Decided where to go next?

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: I'd ask how it feels to have saved the world, but I can guess. The world will keep facing ruin. I wonder what you'll do. It should be interesting.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: I might be part of it myself.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Go on. Keep talking.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: I don't particularly feel like it now. Next time, one bag of rubbish won't be enough.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: Off you go.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Sigh. Can't be helped. I'll leave, then.

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: Then leave...

lines.speaker: 탈로스
lines.text: Sigh... I thought this was about the witches, but apparently not. Still, I'd better be careful...

steps.name: A Stained Fairy Tale (3)
steps.objective: Defeat [Kairos] in 「Kairos's Time」 and obtain the <Storybook: The Witch and the Golem>. Go out to the dungeon's reward room and watch what happens, then turn in the quest to [Theodore] in 「Guild Union City Esnil」.

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: Welcome, Adventurer!

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Have you been well, Narsha? No trouble?

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: No trouble. Since you've been looking out for me, Teacher—I mean, Adventurer—nothing bad has happened lately.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: You're not calling me Teacher anymore?

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: Oh, well... I got told off.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: By whom?

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: Um... The president.

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: He said I should only call someone that when they've actually taught me. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: It's all right. Do you have time to talk?

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: I like talking. What's the matter?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Have you lost anything recently, or been looking for something?

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: I haven't lost anything, but I am looking for something. A book...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: A book?

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: A book containing a story my mother, a Sister, told me when I was little.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Could you tell me the story?
(Narsha closes her eyes and searches her memories.)

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: I don't remember exactly, but it went something like this. A child was walking through a forest and lost their way. Then they met a golem, and the two played together.

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: After several days of playing together, a wicked fairy appeared before the child.

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: The fairy said to stop playing with the golem and return home together. The golem thought it would be better for the child to go with the fairy than stay, and sent the child away...

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: I think it ended with the golem left all alone.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: (...A child and a golem...)

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: Thinking about my situation lately brought the story to mind...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: (It reminds me of Narsha and her magic golem. And of Bergelmir and Eda in Oneiro Forest...)

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: It's an old tale most people here and in the Silvaria Empire know.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: I asked Belpa Library, but they don't have it. It was published so long ago, and so few copies remain, they said it would be hard to find.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: (Could that be the book...?)

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: Adventurer?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Oh, I'll look for it too. I've been traveling somewhere lately... But don't get your hopes up.

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: Thank you just for offering, Teacher. I mean... Adventurer!

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: If you do find it, please give it to Uncle Theo. I think it would be best to have him check it first.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I will. I have somewhere to go, so I'll be off. See you later.

lines.speaker: 나르샤
lines.text: Thank you for visiting when you're so busy.
(As Narsha brightens, the magic golem Madori on her shoulder seems to move excitedly too.)

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Could Kairos help me find the book...? Hmm. Only one way to find out.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Yaaawn... So sleepy.
(Kairos rises from where he was sleeping by the nearby tree and wubs his eyes. Ahem, rubs his eyes.)

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: You're here, mew?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I think I figured out what drifted in here.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Arche told me. What a bother. So what's the thing, mew?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I think it's a book about the friendship between a child and a golem.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: A storybook, mew?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Probably.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: How did you find the object where Chronos was?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: He said it had drifted into a deeper domain, and I needed 'permission.'

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Is that so, mew?

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: This one?
(Kairos pulls a book out of his clothing and waves it.)

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: I was having a nice long sleep without a care, and a book dropped out of the tree. Plop.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Oh, perfect. Give it here. I'll take it out with me.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: But there's a little problem.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Oh, don't tell me...

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: You need permission. It should have drifted into a deeper domain. If it's here, something must have gone awry.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Sigh...

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: How nice not to explain at length. Such a bother... I don't like it either, but we have to spar. Understood, mew?

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Find your way there. I'm off.
(Yawning, Kairos leaps into the tree.)

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Now I'm feeling sleepy too, mew... I want a nap...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Oh, no. Stay focused. Shall we go?

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Sparring over.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Is that enough?

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Here's your book.
(Kairos takes out the book and hands it to %s.)

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: I'm different from that owl clock. I just hand it over without a fuss. Maybe this is an important moment of choice for you, too.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I'm only accepting a book. Why call it important?

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Well...

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Actually, I don't know either. I'm the spirit in charge here, so I felt I should say something like that.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Occupational habit.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Something like that. What's the book about, anyway, mew? I had it, but never read it...

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: It's written in human language, right? Will you read it to me?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Sure. I'm curious too. It's thin, so it shouldn't take long.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Let's see. The title...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: 'The Witch and the Golem.' The witch and the golem?

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Wait, %s! Don't read that here!
(Startled, Kairos snatches the book from %s's hands.)

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Things could get complicated... Lady Gaia wouldn't want that, nor would the being who granted 'permission.'

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: If you want to read it, please do so among humans.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: All right...

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Be careful from now on. We don't know what might happen. Here.
(Looking concerned, Kairos hands the book back.)

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Kairos. This book.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Someone deliberately arranged for it to come here, didn't they?

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: I don't know that much. But you must be careful. I don't know what will happen.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: ...We can't let the moments of fate become tangled. And don't overlook any moment you feel is important.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: All right...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I'll be going, Kairos. Thank you for worrying about me.

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: All right... Go on.
(Only after every trace of the adventurer leaves the Domain of Time does Kairos slowly move away. Then, as if remembering something, he gazes sadly at the sky of time.)

lines.speaker: 카이로스
lines.text: It feels as though the time Lady Gaia feared is slipping through the cracks...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Hello, Theo.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Ah! You're here. Forgive me. I was thinking about something...

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: What brings you here?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I found the book Narsha asked about. She told me to give it to you...

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Oh, did she? May I have it?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Of course. Here...
(Theodore takes the book and leafs through it, then falls silent.)

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: This is an old story familiar to me and many others. Though as an outsider, you may not know it...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: Narsha told me the outline.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: A child lost in a forest meets a golem. They play together until a wicked fairy appears and tells the child to stop playing with it and come home...

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: That's more or less right. The story must have changed little by little as it passed from person to person.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Unlike what Narsha expects, this book seems to preserve much of the original account... Disguised as a fairy tale...

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: It isn't long. I'll briefly explain how I read it.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Freios changed greatly before and after the Sky of Chaos. Wars for dominance saw many powers rise and fall.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: And humans weren't the only ones involved. Human greed exploited other beings too.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Ah, don't repeat this elsewhere. It's something of a taboo...

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: The child wasn't lost. The child had escaped. And they weren't playing with the golem, but desperately avoiding its attacks.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: The fairy tale describes that as playing together...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: What was the wicked fairy?

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: A witch...

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: There are beings called witches in Freios. They are different in nature from the female demons of the Demon Realm. They rarely reveal themselves, but those who do pursue their own affairs.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: To me, the child in this tale seems to be a gift... no, a sacrifice to save a village from the witches.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: The witch probably made the golem, a gatekeeper to prevent the child from escaping. On the surface, it looks like a fairy tale about a child and golem's friendship...

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: But it is simply a witch's story... Perhaps there was something the witch wanted from the child.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Perhaps she wanted the child to become a witch, or recognized that the child already was one...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: That's one way to read it...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: ...Why was Narsha so curious about this book?

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: She probably had a simple desire to understand. Her magic golem, and even her own identity...

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: She must have a lot on her mind...

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Much has happened lately. Sigh... I'll keep this book. I'll find some explanation to give Narsha later.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: All right. And please tell me right away if anything happens to Narsha—or to anyone here.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Aren't you busy enough with your own affairs?

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I'll be fine.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Thank you... If you need my help, come without hesitation.

lines.speaker: %s
lines.text: I'll be going, then. See you again, Theo.

lines.speaker: 태오도르
lines.text: Take care.
(After the adventurer leaves, Theodore examines the book again. His gaze stops on the final page.)

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: Hmm. What do these letters say?

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: An old imperial cipher? I should try putting it together.

lines.speaker: 테오도르
lines.text: 'To Hilda'...? Hilda... Is that someone's name?
